desc:
The string s consists of lowercase letters and the wildcard character ?. A ? may be treated as any lowercase letter you like (each ? independently).

A substring of s is good if, after choosing letters for its wildcards, it contains every character of t with multiplicity, that is, each letter appears in the substring at least as many times as it appears in t. Return the length of the shortest good substring, or -1 if none exists.

s = "ab?ca", t = "abc"
the substring "ab?" works with ? = c, and no 2-character substring has three letters
result = 3
constraints: s contains lowercase letters and ?; t contains only lowercase letters
hints: Without wildcards this is Minimum Window Substring. First think about what condition makes a window good: how many letters of t does the window still lack?
Define the deficit of a window as the sum over letters of max(0, need[c] - count[c]). The window is good exactly when its deficit is at most the number of wildcards in it.

Deficit never rises and the wildcard count never falls when the window grows, so goodness is monotone. Slide two pointers and update the deficit in O(1): adding a letter whose count is still below its need lowers the deficit by one; removing a letter whose count then drops below its need raises it by one.
editorial: A window can be completed with its wildcards precisely when the number of missing letters (the deficit) does not exceed the number of wildcards in it, because each wildcard can fill one missing letter and the letters that are already present need no help. If a window is good, every larger window around it is good as well, which is the structure two pointers need.

Keep cnt[c] for letters in the window, q for wildcards, and deficit starting at len(t). When a letter c enters and cnt[c] < need[c] before the increment, the deficit decreases by one. While deficit <= q, record the window length and remove the left character: for a letter, decrement its count and increase the deficit if the count is now below the need; for a wildcard decrement q. Every character enters and leaves once, so the time is O(n) with O(26) extra space. With no wildcards this is exactly the classic minimum window substring algorithm.
